question_type: sum of five fiscal-year-end cells of one table column (latest printing of each), single value
decisive_step: Two decisions. (1) Table/column: the question's wording ('total Public debt securities ... held by US Government accounts') mirrors OFS-1 'Public debt securities Held by U.S. Government accounts > Total (3)'; the near-duplicate FD-1 column 'Government accounts > Public debt securities (5)' differs from it by a few units every year (FD-1 splits the government-account holdings into public-debt and agency parts). The reference chose OFS-1 by literal header match and logged FD-1 as the alternative (worklog Step 1 and Step 6; solution.structured key_decisions 1). (2) Extraction: each of the five annual cells must be copied as the exact integer printed in the table (reference calc.py CITED block, treasury_bulletin_2009_12.txt:2236-2240; worklog Step 4 confirms only FY2005 was ever revised and the latest printing carries the revised value).

smallest_change.change: printings: print SUMMARY values verbatim instead of '%g'. In otables.py the value keys of the SUMMARY block are built with `"%g" % val` (lines 2208 and 2213), which rounds every number to 6 significant digits and switches to e-notation above 1e6. Replace it with the exact cell text (raw with commas, r/p flags and footnote marks stripped; integers printed in full, decimals kept as printed), and group 'distinct values' on that exact text. The model would then have seen, in a's tailed output, `      <full integer exactly as the cell prints it>: 2006_12..2011_09 (20)` instead of `      <6-digit mantissa>e+06: 2006_12..2011_09 (20)`, and the four values it copied into calc would have been exact.
smallest_change.could_hurt_right_cells: no: b2, c and the reference used exact integers from other outputs; a longer integer on the summary line costs a few bytes per line

fix.why_not_text: Cell a had the provenance sentence ('Before you rely on a value, print the line it comes from') and still summed the rounded summary values, because the summary looked like a tool-printed source. The rounding is invisible to a model that trusts a tool's own summary line; only the tool can stop presenting rounded numbers as values.
fix.irreducible: No. The FD-1 vs OFS-1 choice is a genuine near-duplicate-series ambiguity (the reference records it as its main alternative), but the question wording and the OFS-1 header coincide, and a listing that shows both tables gives the model the same comparison the reference made.

notes: The a/c split on this question is purely output formatting: same table, same column, same latest-printing rule, and a lost 4 of 5 values to the printings SUMMARY '%g' formatting because it tailed the output. Two more latent defects of the same lines: the 'distinct values' count is keyed on the %g string, so two printings that differ beyond 6 significant digits would be reported as 'same in all printings', and a value with more than 6 digits can never be checked against a calc input from the summary. Each per-year printings call prints ~20 near-identical per-issue lines (~2 KB); a compact per-issue listing (issue, value, flags only, one line each, or 'first..latest identical except: ...') would make tailing unnecessary. show_table --grep that matches no row should say why ('no row matches 2005; this part holds rows 2020..June; use --years or printings') instead of 'page rows 0-0 of 0' (a[10], c[12]). find_tables with the question's exact phrase returns 0 results for all four cells because the header says 'Held by U.S. Government accounts' while the question says 'outstanding held by US Government accounts'.
